# K7.4 Evaluation replays the training forward graphs

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

## 1. Packages

G3, G6 and G6b, where named below, are Firmus's earlier GPT-OSS NVFP4 packages (`nemo_g3_nvfp4_v1`, `nemo_g6_nvfp4_v2`,
`nemo_g6b_nvfp4_v2_1`), withdrawn from this submission and no longer in this repository. Their values, line numbers,
images and test jobs are cited as the record of where evidence was collected ([Index](../KERNELS.md), "Earlier packages").

`NVFP4_EVAL_GRAPH=1` (`config_GB300_2x4x3xtp1pp1cp1ep1_nvfp4_v7.sh` L106); 1 in G3, G6 and G6b and G6c.
`NVFP4_EVAL_GRAPH_CHECK` exists but is not set in any of the three configs. Its default is `"0"` (`pretrain.py`
L150), so the check was **not enabled in the scored runs**.
The code is one `pretrain.py` block, the same text in all three (G3 L105–162, G6 and G6b L118–175, G6c L135–192). `pretrain.py` lines
below are G6/G6b; G3 is 13 lines lower, G6c 17 lines higher. Class: **Bitwise**.

## 2. What the reference does

Megatron-LM `f6c33bde` replays the per-layer TE CUDA graphs (K7.3) only in training mode. In evaluation
(`model.eval()`, `no_grad`) each layer runs its eager forward. The evaluation loop is unchanged: every
`VAL_CHECK_INTERVAL` = 512 steps, `VAL_SAMPLES` = 1024 samples (config L197–198), `eval_iters`
from `conf/gpt_oss.yaml` L13–14.
G6c changes which samples are scored, not the forward: `evaluate_on_fixed_validation_window` (`pretrain.py`
L1019–1031, called at L1536–1538) builds the validation loader over the first `eval_iters × global_batch_size`
samples, sequentially, so every evaluation scores the same samples.

## 3. What this implementation does

The block finds Megatron's graphable module class (the one defining `_should_call_te_cudagraph`, L127–131) and wraps
its `__call__` (L146–175). It replays the captured graph when the module is not training, has graphs, grad is
disabled, `cuda_graph_impl == "transformer_engine"` and no capture is running (L147–153). `_replay_in_eval` (L136–144)
then clears the module's manual hooks (the per-layer param all-gather hooks), sets `training=True`, and calls
`_te_cuda_graph_replay`. It restores both afterwards. Otherwise the original call runs (L173).

With `NVFP4_EVAL_GRAPH_CHECK=n`, the first n eligible calls run both the eager eval forward and the replay. Each prints
`NVFP4_EVAL_GRAPH_CHECK rank r layer l bitwise <bool> max_abs ... rel_l2 ...` and returns the replay result
(L154–172). The replay result is returned because K7.3's chained IO requires each layer graph's input to be the previous
graph's output (comment L156–158).

## 4. Why the result is the same

The training-mode forward and the eval-mode forward compute the same function here:

- dropout is 0: `hidden_dropout=0.0`, `attention_dropout=0.0` (`pretrain.py` L1083–1084; scored log
  `attention_dropout: 0.0`, `hidden_dropout: 0.0`);
- no forced load balancing: `MOE_ROUTER_FORCE_LOAD_BALANCING=False` (config L63);
- no expert bias: `moe_router_enable_expert_bias=False` in the scored log's config dump.

The graph replays the kernels captured from the training-mode forward. Where training mode selects a different kernel,
that kernel must be bitwise equal to the eval path. In this package the training-only paths are K8.4's residual add
(`_ResidualAdd`, V7 patch L2294–2299, `residual + x` as the plain add) and K10.3's unpermute with the residual (set only in training, `firmus_kernels/resgrad_fwd_nobias.py` L106–107), both Bitwise; K5.4 is off. Evaluation reads only the forward outputs (the loss);
the backward state the replay writes is discarded. Bitwise, as measured below.

## 5. Numerics

The formats of the training forward (K2.1, K2.2, K2.3; G6/G6b/G6c also K8.1). The forward uses round-to-nearest casts;
stochastic rounding applies to gradients, which evaluation does not compute.

## 6. Shapes and fallbacks

- **Gate:** L147–153 (eval mode, graphs present, grad off, TE graph implementation, not capturing).
- **Falls back:** eager evaluation forward (L173), silently.
- **Assumes:**
  - Parameters are already gathered when evaluation starts. The replay skips the param all-gather hooks (L137–138;
    comment L122–123). If the evaluation loop did not force a param sync, the replay would read parameters from an
    unfinished all-gather. The package does not check this.
  - Evaluation micro-batches have the captured shape (micro-batch 3 × 8192 tokens).
  - The captured forward keeps no state across calls that affects later training. The replay does re-run K6.3's
    captured weight cast on unchanged weights.
- **Check:** config L106. The scored logs have no line from this block, because it prints
  only in check mode. They do show `eval_accuracy` lines every 512 steps and the graph capture (K7.3).

## 7. Code

`nemo_g6c_nvfp4_v2_2/pretrain.py` L135–192.

## 8. Tests and evidence

- **Package check, G6 image, test run (package config plus check switches):** job 22171, 2 × 4 GPUs, 544 steps, so one
  evaluation. `NVFP4_EVAL_GRAPH_CHECK`: 24 of 24 layers bitwise.
  The check on this package's image follows.
- **Package check, this package's image (package config plus check switches):** job 22923, 2 × 4 GPUs, 544 steps,
  evaluation at step 512, `NVFP4_EVAL_GRAPH_CHECK=48`: 24 of 24 layers `bitwise True`, `max_abs 0`, `rel_l2 0` (rank 0,
  first evaluation; `../KERNELS.md` section 9.2).
- Job 22298 (450 steps) set `NVFP4_EVAL_GRAPH_CHECK=48` but ran no evaluation (interval 512), so it printed nothing.
- **Development record (development repository):** job 19760, first evaluation, rank 0: 24 layers bitwise, on the
  G3-era development path (`pretrain_fp4_param_v24.py`), not a submitted image.
